title: How to Benchmark Vision Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation?
mechanism: Benchmark protocol study: ViT-B, patch 16, linear decoder ranks VFMs like costlier settings; linear probing does not predict fine-tune ranking; rankings shift across datasets and domain shifts.
evidence: R (abstract): settings cut training time over 13x with representative rankings; promptable-segmentation pretraining not beneficial, MIM with abstract targets important.
adaptation: Use to (a) argue our frozen linear-probe nulls do not close fine-tune or PEFT arms, and (b) define the VFM part of the EL benchmark protocol, testing whether a linear decoder is representative for 1-2 px cracks.
min_experiment: Rank 3 VFMs with ViT-B linear-decoder fine-tune and with VFM-H; check rank agreement on CV crack relF1@2; no kill, protocol check.
prior_overlap: Not a method; informs reading of the closed probe row.
